_comment: GOLDEN-SET TEMPLATE. Copy this file to '<shipment>.json' (drop the leading underscore so the runner picks it up) and fill it in for one real past shipment. See eval/README.md. Every '_comment*' key is documentation and is ignored by the runner.
title: Short human label for this shipment
notes: Free text: what makes this shipment interesting (2-in-1 file? scan? multi-item? tri-party?).
_comment_documents: One entry per document in the shipment. In DRY-RUN the runner reads 'fixture'; in --real it reads 'source'. 'expected' holds ONLY the fields you hand-verified — leave out anything you didn't check.

documents._comment_source: Used in --real mode. Either a path to the real file (relative to the repo root or absolute) OR pasted plain text.
documents._comment_fixture: Used in DRY-RUN mode: a recorded extraction JSON (a full ExtractedFields object), path relative to eval/fixtures/. Record one with --real once you trust the extraction, or write it by hand.
documents._comment_expected: The correct values. doc_type + numbers exact; currency case-insensitive; hs_code compared on digits only; weights/values/counts within EVAL_NUM_TOLERANCE (default 1%). also_contains is a set.

_comment_expected_discrepancies: The discrepancies reconcile() SHOULD report for this shipment (ground truth). 'field' is required and must be a discrepancy field name (po_number, net_weight_kg, gross_weight_kg, total_weight_kg, packages_count, currency, total_value, hs_code, country_of_origin, incoterm, seller, buyer, line_items). 'kind' (confirmed=red / suspected=yellow) and 'severity' are optional — if omitted, matching is by field only. An empty array means a clean shipment.

expected_discrepancies.note: no HS code on the invoice — yellow verify flag
